text:
olivia: Hey finance — got invoice from NordicData AB (SE) for $12,400. They charged 25% Swedish VAT but their VAT ID doesn't match VIES. Vendor is asking if we can 'gross-up' the payment to cover VAT while they sort registration. Thoughts?

emma: Can you paste the invoice fields and vendor portal link? Want to see line items and VAT breakouts.

olivia: Invoice snippet: 
```
Vendor: NordicData AB
Vendor VAT: SE556677889901
Invoice#: ND-2026-337
Amount ex VAT: 9,920
VAT charged @25%: 2,480
Total: 12,400
```
Portal: https://vendors.example.com/nordicdata/invoice/ND-2026-337

karim: Quick tax take — we should avoid grossing-up by default. If this is cross-border B2B within EU the correct treatment is usually reverse charge (buyer accounts for VAT). If their VAT number fails VIES they may have incorrectly charged VAT. We need proof of their VAT registration or a corrected invoice. :thinking:

tax-ops: Ran an auto VIES check — result: no match for SE556677889901 (VIES returned empty). Recommendation: 1) Request vendor VAT registration certificate or Swedish Bolagsverket extract; 2) Request corrected invoice without Swedish VAT referencing reverse charge / Article 196 and include our VAT ID; 3) If vendor insists on being paid VAT, get written justification and escalate to tax counsel.

emma: If we hold the VAT portion, any AP/GL impact we should beware of? Can we pay the net amount and hold VAT in a suspense account until they reissue?

karim: Operationally that's OK but increases reconciliation work. Paying gross-up increases our cost baseline and complicates refunds if they later correct the invoice. Strong preference: ask for corrected invoice. If they refuse and provide evidence they're not VAT registered, then they shouldn’t charge VAT — still need docs.

olivia: I'll reply to vendor asking for VAT certificate + corrected invoice that references reverse charge and our VAT ID. I'll CC legal/tax. Wording: "Please provide proof of Swedish VAT registration or reissue the invoice net of VAT with the statement 'Reverse charge — Article 196, buyer to self-account'. Until we receive documentation we will not gross up the payment."

emma: Good. If vendor pushes back, loop in legal and we can consider a one-off with indemnity.

olivia: Sending now. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
